html:
The downtown farmers market doubled the value of food assistance benefits spent at its stalls last season, and vendors sold $212,000 in produce through the match.

Shoppers using benefits could get up to $25 in extra tokens each visit, which were good only for fruits and vegetables.

The number of households using the match grew from 640 in the first season to 1,510 last year, according to the market's annual report.

Farmers said the program brought in new regular customers, and eleven vendors reported that benefit sales made up more than a fifth of their market revenue.

The match is funded by a federal nutrition incentive grant and two local hospitals, which together contributed $95,000 last year.

The market plans to extend the match to its winter indoor market, which runs every other Saturday from December through March.
